notes:
1. BI page — Relationships: link warehouse tables on a shared column (left or inner join), drill from a row to its related rows in the linked table, or view a flat joined table; relationships are saved, editable and deletable.
2. Relationship diagram: all relationships in one view — tables as nodes connected by lines labelled with the key pair, colored/solid for left joins and dashed green for inner joins, with arrows showing direction; hover a line for details.
3. Charts across tables: in the Chart tab, pick a relationship as the chart data source to chart fields from both tables at once (joined dataset, up to 5,000 rows).
4. Warehouse section: snapshots and relationships combined into one tabbed, collapsible card with live counts.
5. Edit grid window: AI edit, data types and calculated columns combined into a single dialog with tabs; the data types tab redesigned as responsive cards with a per-column type dropdown.
6. Snapshots: one-click button to load stored rows back into the Query grid.

1. Query grid — smarter copy: with a drill-through filter active, the Copy button now exports only the rows you can see (the drilled-down set) instead of the whole result; row selections still take priority.
2. Summary tab — sortable table: click any column header (group-by columns, Column name, or a statistic) to sort the table; clicking again flips the direction, a third click returns to the original order. Copy and Download Excel follow the sorted order.
3. Summary drill-through: clicking a row in the Summary table or pivot now scrolls the Query page smoothly to the results grid, so the drilled rows are in view as soon as you land.
4. About page: two new info cards show the technology behind the app — the frontend stack (React · MUI · AG Grid · ECharts) and the backend stack (Python · FastAPI · pyodbc · pandas).

1. Workspace — live feedback: query results now fade in with a soft staggered animation while a skeleton placeholder shows during the run; the Run button flips to a green Done tick on success and a shaking red Failed on error; KPI numbers count up to their value and the cards lift slightly on hover.
2. Message pop-ups — success colour: success toasts (reconnect, upload, connection test, AI test) now use a bright green background with dark text for a clearer "all good" signal; errors keep their own distinct style.
3. Feedback window: the Discussion window now has the same rounded corners as the reply box (an oversized-corner glitch is fixed), shows a progress bar at the top while a post's content is being fetched, and adds Previous / Next buttons above the message — with a position counter — so you can step through the board's feedback in order.
4. Script tab: the data-source card stacks its controls in full-width rows on wide screens too (matching the narrow layout), and the View button now sits on the same row as the Template dropdown.

1. Chart area — histogram binning: the bin-count slider is replaced by a Bin size box plus Start and End boxes. Leave them blank to auto-fit the data (10 even buckets), type a bin size to set the bucket width, or set a start/end range to clip the domain — values outside the range are dropped.
2. Message bar: pop-up messages (upload, save, errors) now sit on a dark green background, with a larger, rounder close button centred against the text so it is easier to hit on both desktop and touch screens.

1. Results grid — paste data: a new Paste button sits next to Upload, and Ctrl+V pastes straight from Excel. When the grid already holds rows the paste replaces them (Revert undoes it); a pasted header row becomes the table's column names, and empty rows are dropped.
2. Chart area — secondary Y axis: bar, stacked bar, trend, step line, area, stacked area and combo charts now offer the Y2 (secondary) shelf, so a second measure is plotted on its own right-hand axis (the top axis for horizontal bars).
3. Chart area — Visualizations pane: the chart type panel now collapses and expands sideways into a slim rail on the right, matching the Fields rail, instead of folding up and down.
4. Chart area — column types: a column type changed in the results grid is reflected in the chart builder's column panel straight away, and a saved BI snapshot keeps the types its columns had.
5. Laminate Lab Results (analyze-tautona-data): the script now opens a native Windows dialog first, listing every test component (ANALYSIS + RESULT_NAME) so unwanted ones can be unchecked; set LAMINATE_SKIP_PICKER=1 to analyze everything without the dialog.
